text:
olivia: Heads-up — after merging PR #4123 the prod-canary shows a decode tail latency increase ~20% on 2nd-gen A100 nodes. Noticed during the 02:10 deploy window.
ci-bot: [auto] Perf check failed on canary: +18% p99_decode_time vs baseline (baseline: 12ms -> now: 14.2ms). Link: https://ci.redwood/perf/1768809999 :warning:
olivia: Snapshot of the flame graph attached (quick paste):
```
# flamegraph snippet
decode_step -> attention_kernel_dispatch -> kv_memcopy -> fused_op_execute
heavy: attention_kernel_dispatch (45%)
```
samir: Can you paste the kernel selector debug for a sample request? I want to see if it switched kernels post-merge.
olivia: Sure — here's one trace where it picked the fallback attention kernel (note the flags):
```
selected_kernel: attention_v2_fallback
reason: failed_quantized_path_checks
heuristics: seq_len=256, batch=1, kv_mem_mb=1024
```
jen: That "failed_quantized_path_checks" looks new. PR #4123 changed the kernel probe ordering right? It moved some heuristics earlier.
dina: I ran a local microbench: before merge attention_v1 (optimized) was chosen; after merge selector prefers attention_v2_fallback for certain seq distributions. p50 ~ same, but p99 shifts.
mike: Also seeing increased memcpy counts in KV cache stats. Command output: `rdw-kv-stats --window 5m`
```
kv_memcopies: 214k -> 334k
average_kv_copy_size: 128kb -> 192kb
cache_hits: 89.4% (unchanged)
```
olivia: So cache hit ratio stable but we're doing more/more expensive memcopies. Could be the kernel change increases KV read stride causing extra copies.
samir: Can we bisect to the specific commit? I started a git-bisect on the canary branch and narrowed it to commits 0c4a..e1b7 (suspect area around kernel ordering + fused ops).
jen: If it's the heuristic reordering we should be able to reproduce with a unit test that asserts kernel selection for model X on seq=256. Can someone add that?
mike: I've got a perf build running with added counters: `ATTN_KERNEL=1 KV_MEMCOPY_BYTES` should land in ~20m. I'll dump the traces.
perf-bot: Perf job 1768810600 completed: attention_v2_fallback has 2.1x higher avg_kv_memcopy_bytes vs attention_v1 on the same workload. Details: https://perf.redwood/jobs/1768810600
dina: Repro script (local): `python scripts/repro_sel.py --model redwood-l3 --seq 256 --batch 1 --seed 42` produces fallback selection after 3 runs consistently.
jen: Proposal: revert the probe-order change in #4123 to restore prior selection while we patch heuristics. Any objections? :thinking_face:
samir: +1 from me. It's blocking canary rollout; we should revert to stop customer impact.
mike: I'll open the revert PR and also include a short test so CI will catch regressions.
olivia: Thanks — please also add a perf regression CI job that checks p99 decode for a small suite. We missed this because only average latency was checked.
ci-bot: Revert PR #4123-r1 opened by mike. CI: running perf checks.
perf-bot: [auto] CI perf guard detected p99 increase on the revert branch as well — investigating anomaly (possible noise).
samir: If CI still noisy, we need to tighten the test harness (fixed seeds, warmed-up KV cache, fixed batch patterns).
jen: I'll own adding a determinism mode for perf tests in CI. Will post a PR.
dina: For root cause follow-up: checklist — add kernel selection unit test, add KV memcpy counters to perf suite, add p99 guard in CI, revert in place until heuristics fixed.
olivia: Agreed. Rolling back canary and pausing rollout now. :raised_hands:
mike: Revert merged and rolled back canary at 12:23 UTC. Monitoring dashboards: no further p99 spikes seen in the last 20m.
olivia: Great work everyone — let's sync tomorrow 10am to split follow-ups. :calendar:)
